title: Loads are watched from telemetry, not a log file

statements.says: Two hooks post the record themselves: SessionStart writes one record for the session, and InstructionsLoaded writes one Load per file.
Both records go to the Collector already running for Studio, which forwards them to Loki.
An alarm that knows which rules it expected and says so when one is missing is deferred, not refused.
The hook is written for node.
The hook has a time limit of its own, 2 s, well under the 5 s hook limit.
One time limit covers both the git call that finds the Repository and the post.
When the time limit runs out, the hook stops git, sends nothing, and exits zero.
SKILLWORKS_WATCH_LIMIT_MS sets another limit.
The tests set a long limit, except the tests of the limit itself.
A hook that fails says nothing, and nothing in this decision fixes that.
The endpoint is read from OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, which is already set where telemetry is on.
This is for local development, and a machine with no Collector is not served.
None of the readers of the rules says which rules a session was actually given.
CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_MDS=1 takes the rules away while printing nothing, so a week with no rules can look exactly like a week with them.
Claude Code emits no telemetry of its own that names an instruction file.
The pair of records keeps two facts apart: a session record with no Loads says the rules did not arrive, and no records at all says the Collector was not there.
The hook is handed session_id and prompt_id, the same values Claude Code puts on every telemetry event, so the join to the session already exists.
A record first leaves the alarm buildable on top.
The alarm waits because the expected set is a second truth that can rot, and it would be guessed before anyone has read a week of real Loads.
The hook takes about 100 ms under node and about 750 ms under PowerShell, and PowerShell has to be installed on macOS and Linux.
The setup ships to machines that are not this one, so the slower runtime would cost every one of them.
A Collector that takes the connection and never answers would otherwise hold the first answer of every Session until the 5 s hook limit ran out.
The limit was 1 s at first, but on a busy machine git alone could take longer and the record was lost.
The tests set a long limit so that how busy the machine is cannot decide whether a test passes.
A log file was rejected, because the records would sit where nothing else can read them and joining them to a session would be work done by hand.
A span in Tempo was rejected, because there is usually no span yet at session start, which is the moment the rules load.
InstructionsLoaded alone was rejected, because it cannot report an absence: zero files loaded is zero events.
